# dsh-split-session

A DeepSeek Harness Web plugin that turns the main window into a **quad session
view**: up to four li

ve Conversations in one window, each pane running a native
embedded Conversation (not an iframe, not

a copied transcript). It opens by
default at launch, and Sessions can be dragged in from the sideba

copied transcript). It opens by
default at launch, and Sessions can be dragged in from the sidebar.

## Features

- **2 to 4 panes, one window.** Add panes up to a 2×2 quad; close any pane back
down to two. Layouts

: side-by-side, stacked, two-over-one, quad.
- **Native Conversations.** Each pane binds its own Ses

sion reference through
the standard `SessionProvider` seat and renders the Conversation package's
pu

blic `conversation.content` Factory in its `embedded` variant. Streaming,
the composer, slash comman

ds, approvals, queued turns, todos, and plugin views
all work per pane.
- **Fuzzy drag targets.** Dr

ag any Session row onto the panel: every pane shows
its half/quarter label, the zone under the point

er lights up, and a wide dead
band along both dividers keeps the target from flickering. Dropping on

e
pane's Session on another swaps them.
- **Launch by default.** The panel is the main view at page

launch, and the
current workspace group is expanded in the sidebar so rows are ready to drag.
- **Re

size both axes.** Drag the column and row dividers, use the arrow keys on
a focused divider, `Home`/

double-click to reset one axis.
- **Per-pane picker.** Click a pane title to switch that pane, with

running
spinners and the other panes' Sessions excluded.
- **Persists.** Pane list, both axis ratios

, and the two-pane orientation live
in `localStorage`; the layout survives reloads.
- **Focus-safe.*

* Opening or switching a pane does not yank the keyboard into
its composer.
- **Dark/light and Engli
sh/Chinese** through the host's theme and locale.

## Use

- **Add a pane**: the grid `+` button in the panel header, up to four panes.
- **Close a pane**: the

✕ in a pane's title row (available while more than two
panes are open).
- **Switch a pane**: click

its title; the picker lists top-level Sessions by
recent activity.
- **Drag a Session in**: drag a r

ow from the sidebar onto any pane. Each pane
labels its half or quarter and highlights under the poi

nter; drag a pane's
Session onto another pane to swap them.
- **Add by dropping**: while fewer than

four panes are open, move the drag onto
the panel header — it becomes a **Drop to add a pane** lane

— and release to
add the dragged Session as a new pane. Repeat to build the quad, then drop
Sessions

into the labeled quarters.
- **Resize**: drag a divider, focus it and use the arrow keys (±2%), pre

ss
`Home` or double-click to reset that axis.
- **Side-by-side / stacked**: for two panes, the panel

header toggles the axis.
- **Swap**: exchange the two panes (two-pane layouts).
- **Close the view*

*: the header ✕ returns to the Conversation without changing
the selected Session.

The layout persists per browser in `localStorage` under
`dsh.split-session.v2` (the two-pane `v1` la
yout migrates automatically).

## How it composes
The package has no Host behavior. Its browser half:

1. registers a `main` panel keyed `split` plus the `sidebar.panellist` entry;
2. declares one sessio

n-scoped child slot, `split.pane`
(`{ kind: 'single', scope: 'session' }`), whose occupant renders t
ays the panes out on one CSS grid with two ratiometric dividers.

It never imports another feature plugin's values: the Conversation arrives
through a Factory, Sessio

n state through standard seats, and Session retention
through the `sessions` service. It requests no

non-baseline modules — React and
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` come from the shell's shar

ed module
table — so the package needs no `dsh.client.external` declaration.

Launching selects the panel once per page lifetime (the tag is the page's
`performance.timeOrigin`,

so a browser reload re-opens it and a bundle reload
does not), then expands the current workspace gr

oup that the sidebar's own
Conversation-only effect would otherwise have expanded. Drag-and-drop rid

es the
sidebar's own draggable rows: the panel listens for `dragstart` on
`[data-row-key^="session:"

]`, tracks the pointer over its own surface, and
assigns the nearest pane — it never modifies the si
debar's rows or order.
## Alternatives

The split-view space already has capable plugins; this one is deliberately
smaller and native-render

split-view space already has capable plugins; this one is deliberately
smaller and native-rendered:
| Plugin | Shape |
| `mhlywxl/dsh-split-workspace` | Unlimited native panes, side-by-side, stacked, 2×2 and automatic g

rids. Closest overlap. |
| `dsh-split-screen` | Native panes, drag-to-edge splitting, many panes, al

ways-on workspace. |
| `dsh-split-view` | Nested splits, one full DSH client per iframe, hibernation

, settings. |
| `@syncended/dsh-split-screen` | iTerm-style multiplexer, nested splits, tabs, up to

12 panes. |
| `yuloop/dsh-web-split` | Draggable panes with unread dots and per-browser layout. |
|
**dsh-split-session** | Quad cap, native embedded Conversations, launch-default, sidebar drag, zero
on** | Quad cap, native embedded Conversations, launch-default, sidebar drag, zero external peers. |
